The working file is the complete analysis; the reports are its reader copies. Each should be read in full — this message is not the analysis.

Bottom line: the efficiency premise fails decisively and the cost premise is genuinely open, not confirmed either way. A 290–565 °C molten-salt system converting electricity→heat→electricity cannot exceed roughly 65% round-trip efficiency under any architecture located in the literature (the Carnot ceiling for a simple design is ~64%; the best real-world pilot at comparable scale, SPIC's 1 MW/4 MWh unit, tops out "over 65%") — nowhere near the claimed 85%+. That finding is rated HIGH confidence, built entirely on five independently-sourced, read-at-source figures with no unverified inputs. Cost-competitiveness at 5 MWh is rated MEDIUM: the power-conversion block plausibly dominates capex at this small scale, and the resulting cost bracket straddles the Li-ion comparison point rather than resolving it (the open question is a vendor-specific power-block cost quote this analysis couldn't obtain). A third, independent defect: "same nameplate capacity" isn't even a well-posed comparison, since TES decouples power rating from energy capacity far more than Li-ion does (also HIGH confidence).
